summary: Completed the Node-wrapper question on its final receipt. CheckRun c53145c01ad94b449ca1c8b81fe8d7b4 (fixed experiment 2318a1c9ee5d4b76995a322bd4bfcf06-experiment, version 3) parsed seven events with no loss and resolved all nine comparisons: the two controls hold (parsed index 1 - before the removal Propose returns no error in 0ms with the leader's log index at 2), the two premises hold on the witness event (index 4 - the leader's configuration contains node 2 again and the node still knows leader 1 in term 1), the two witness assertions are violated (index 4 - Propose returns only when its 300ms deadline fires and the leader's log index stays at 4), and the three restore comparisons hold (index 5 - the wrapped node reports StateLeader at term 2; index 6 - the same call returns no error in 0ms and its commit index advances 5 to 6). The account therefore states the full arc on one conforming prefix: the proposal channel works before the removal, stays closed after the re-add while the same leader remains, and re-opens exactly when the leadership changes - the only repair mechanism the source provides - so the defect is a lost member duty bounded by the leadership rather than permanent. The restore path moves from an unmeasured limitation to a measured bound, the earlier receipts remain history (the persistence-tainted one withdrawn as evidence, the intermediate one superseded), and the question's discriminator was replaced by the remaining open point: whether an application can detect the closed channel other than through its own context deadline, and whether other membership sequences reach the same state. Counterevidence keeps the holding controls, the measured restore path, the documented proposal-loss caveat and the fact that the behaviour reproduced unchanged on the corrected prefix; limitations keep the one-sided wrapper harness, the 300ms deadline, the untested other membership sequences, and the open question of the wrapper's intended semantics for a re-added node.
